> It will be a single board PCB that senses its environment and responds accordingly. I will attach a temperature/humidity sensor, and a noise sensor. There will also be a set of conditions for a healthy environment. Whilst either of the conditions are met, a happiness meter will go up, and it will go faster if they are both suitable. There is going to be an OLED with a changing face to make users feel like they need to improve their wellbeing. This is a good project for me because it will be a bit challenging to make, and also fun to have as a pet robot.

### 2026-10-08: I watched a tutorial (I really should have the first time) and learnt a lot of new things about PCB design. The main thing I learnt is that I had done almost everything wrong and had to redesign the s

**5h**

I watched a tutorial (I really should have the first time) and learnt a lot of new things about PCB design. The main thing I learnt is that I had done almost everything wrong and had to redesign the schematic and routed board. I redesigned the schematic with parts from the common library as well, and also made sure there weren't any overlapping wires as in the first.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 164526](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/50914216d511f0977b6035c5c52ba538c4d8bf755001595d144f0a5afd0a2050.png)

Then I played around with positions and layer counts for the PCB to make sure every track could be auto routed. This took some time and iterations but I finally landed on a good layout. I also added some text saying Hexbie, and made the board shape a hexagon... or as I would say BESTAGON.

I added the required things to my Github repository and learnt a lot about how to use github. (This is the first time I have made a repository) I added the PCB cost to the parts list and ordered it from JLCPCB so that it will arrive in time for the making week of this project. I also purchased the items off of Aliexpress because I was worried that they would go out of stock or change prices as they waited in my cart. The other items are at Jaycar next to my school so I can pick them up whenver, really. I also made the 5h reel.

### 2026-10-09: I re-wrote the code so that it is more user friendly and will work better. I looked through different options for creating bitmaps for my OLED and chose KasperCalc. I drew up 3 frames for each of the

**4h**

I re-wrote the code so that it is more user friendly and will work better. I looked through different options for creating bitmaps for my OLED and chose KasperCalc. I drew up 3 frames for each of the 4 happiness levels (A total of 12 frames) and then put them into a google doc. From that, I attached them to the different frames in my code. With my remade code, it has two screens that show on the OLED. One of them has the sound level, temperature, and air quality so that the user knows how much they need to improve the environment. The other screen has a series of animation presets that change depending on the bot's "Happiness". The happiness is how many of the input variables are suitable for a good working environment. It took a lot of time to animate but now I've finished my project.

**2.5h**

This was a very tedious task, and I had to be careful to make sure the board didn't get exposed to heat for too long. Then, I tested out the basic blink to make sure it was working.

![Screenshot 2026-11-10 164530](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/610ae61ec5888425b29bfa53b2568989940bef2dd1a9585bdeda5d0b41e1e82d.png)

I grabbed a bread board and placed down the parts that I have for the project. Then, I connected them up. I actually don't have many dupont cables and very minimal other cables so it doesn't look good and there are unnecessary connections to extend length.

![WhatsApp Image 2026-11-10 at 4.42.50 PM 1](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/398bdef88cfe522963286914686541be476d9b2a32e75ab629f7cc9d3beba53d.jpg)

![WhatsApp Image 2026-11-10 at 4.42.50 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/2ced419fe49a5d5de09419c3a873e6230cbfffc29aed509bba59cf6e3244fac7.jpg)

I tried uploading my code from Steamakersblocks.com but it took up too much space with all of the bitmaps for the OLED.

![Screenshot 2026-11-09 172514](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/9b7eb227b5a512f618f46ea93c09e2cd8c10185650d539b24022003204b397f6.png)

 I removed some bitmaps but it was still at a high percentage of the storage. When I uploaded the code, nothing changed on the OLED so I knew something must still be wrong. I checked the OLED by connecting another nano I had lying around and it wrote to the OLED fine.

![WIN_20261110_17_01_06_Pro](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/6mG7f89ZDOsngQ8qn0yp6oxaSBtp0k8c/7736a6e8dbb5cf5b477a8de7bd9bc68753f1ec128859b93f7d34c6d946c19fd8.jpg)

I did some searching on the internet and it's because Steamakersblocks adds huge libraries when using parts, which is unnecesary for what I am doing.  This might have also caused compatibility issues with the nano and the parts.

My next steps are writing the same code in Arduino IDE to hopefully reduce the sketch size and possible compatibility issues.

### 2026-11-11: I wrote out the code in Arduino IDE, using help from lots of libraries and references online. I went through a bunch of errors but they were all very easy to fix. On the OLED screen, the face wasn't s

**2h**

I wrote out the code in Arduino IDE, using help from lots of libraries and references online. I went through a bunch of errors but they were all very easy to fix. On the OLED screen, the face wasn't showing up fully, and it wasn't covering the whole screen. I found this was because I put 128x32 somewhere instead of 128x64. I changed this and that fixed the issue. Another issue was that the animations weren't playing. This is because I didn't clear them after the first one, so the other one stayed on top. I fixed that and then the animations sort of worked. Now, the eyes would stay shut instead of opening and closing how I would like them to. I couldn't figure out why this was so I instead swapped out a bitmap to at least keep the eyes there, only smaller. I also took out the display because the numbers would be from 0 to 1023 and confusing to interpret.
